newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Surgutneftegaz to hold oil port tender.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Surgutneftegaz to hold oil port tender.

text.p: NK Surgutneftegaz will hold a tender for the right to construct an oil port in Batareinaya Bay, in the Gulf of Finland, the deputy head of the Leningrad region construction committee said on Friday.
Vladimir Smirnov told Reuters both Russian and foreign firms would be able to participate.
He said the main contruction work should be completed by 2000, when annual throughput will be 7.5 million tonnes of refined oil products. Its projected annual capacity is 15 million tonnes, he said.
The overall port construction cost is over $200 million.

Surgutneftegaz, whose Kirishi refinery will be one of the main suppliers to the port, also plans to build temporary electricity lines, water pipes, railway and automobile roads, and deepen the bottom of the bay, Smirnov said.
The Leningrad region administration also plans to attract investors to create a system of safe sailing and to build rail and automobile roads to the port.
NK Surgutneftegaz is one of a dozen vertically integrated Russian oil groups, whose main production unit is Surgutneftegaz.
